To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the axial‐annural flow reactor configuration is an effective means for the hydrolysis (conversion to glucose and galactose) of the lactose constituent in skim milk.
an immobilized β‐Gal enzyme reactor was used to hydrolyse skim milk.
the immobilized enzyme reactor is a promising technology for the continuous hydrolysis of milk lactose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hydrolysis and removal of lactose from skim milk by using immobilized β‐d‐galactoside galactohydrolase (β‐galactosidas).
the development of a reactor for the enzymatic hydrolysis of skim milk.
the hydrolysis kinetics of lactose in the skim milk matrix.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the axial‐annual flow immobilized β‐Galactosidase system is an excellent reactor for the hydrolysis and removal of lactose from skim milk.
the axial‐annulair flow reactor is an effective and practical means of hydrolyzing the lactose component in skim milk.
a three‐parameter competitive inhibition model is sufficient to describe the enzymatic hydrolysis of skim milk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immobilized enzyme axial‐annular reactor can be used for the hydrolysis (or partial hydrolysis) of the lactose constituent in skim milk.
the immobilized enzyme reactor is a viable means for the production of lactose‐free dairy products.
the immobilized β‐Gal reactor is an effective means of hydrolyzing the lactose constituent in skim milk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the axial‐annulair reactor is a good reactor for hydrolyzing the lactose in the skim milk.
the axial‐annual flow reactor is capable of hydrolyzing the lactose component in skim milk without any of the problems that have plagued other reactor configurations.
immobilized β‐Galactosidase can be used to effectively hydrolyze the constituent lactose of skim milk in a continuous reactor system.
